newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, late buying trims losses.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, late buying trims losses.

text.p: Late buying in the July contract helped KCBT hard red winter wheat futures climb off their daily lows and end mixed, traders said.

KCBT wheat weakened amid sizeable bear-spreading that was linked to fund activity, traders said. KCBT wheat also drew pressure from forecasts for more moisture Tuesday and Wednesday in HRW growing areas of the southern U.S. Plains.

Refco, a commission house tied to large fund holdings, bear-spread 3.5 million May/March bushels. E. D. & F. Man International reportedly was on the other side of that spread, but Man also bear-spread three million July/March bushels.
Traders said the late short-covering came from commission house FIMAT, which bought around 700,000 July bushels after having sold two million July earlier.
KCBT wheat closed 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 cents higher, with March down 6-1/2 cents at $4.31. May lost 4-1/4 cents to close at $4.03-1/4.

U.S. wheat markets suffered early after Sparks Companies Analyst Brad Anderson, in remarks prepared for USDA's annual Outlook Forum, pegged U.S. wheat output at 2.44 billion bushels, above the updated USDA outlook for 2.27 billion.
